summary: The memos session gate cannot be opened by the application's own sign-in flow, so no behind-the-gate journey can be written truthfully. Signin.tsx validates email AND password with maxLength 24 before calling api.login; the frozen seed's owner email is 34 chars and MEMOS_OWNER_PASSWORD is 26, so both are refused client-side and login is never issued. Signup is unreachable because the seed holds an OWNER, so /api/status reports one and the button renders 'Sign in'. All four required journeys live behind that gate. Fixing it requires changing the frozen seed, which moves the 1672b43f behavior digest — a drift the packet forbids. No files written.
open_questions: Should the frozen projection seed be amended so the owner credential pair passes the pinned client's own validator (minLength 4, maxLength 24, noSpace) — e.g. email 'owner@evidence.invalid' (22 chars) and MEMOS_OWNER_PASSWORD 'synthetic-pass' (14 chars)? This necessarily moves seedSha256, MEMOS_PROJECTION_BEHAVIOR_DIGEST off 1672b43f, and the projection block of evidence/runs/react-memos-v0-1-3/t006-api-surface.json.

If the seed must stay frozen, is there a sanctioned alternative for opening the gate that is still the application's own flow? I found none: appRouter has only /signin and *->Home, Home gates unconditionally on GET /api/user/me, POST /api/user needs a prior session, and profile.mode 'prod' means the dev prefill (demo@usememos.com/secret) never fires and would 401 regardless.

Should u12 be re-cut as two units — one amending the seed and re-freezing the digest plus the enumeration record, then one witnessing the journeys — given the digest change also touches the u11 enumeration facts?
